urgency.label: Urgency
urgency.definition: The scammer sets a short deadline so you act before you can think or ask anyone.
signs: "Within 24 hours", "today only" or "last chance"
A warning that something bad happens if you wait, such as a closed account
Pressure to reply or pay right now
A request to keep it secret so nobody can stop you
urgency.how_it_works: When you are in a rush, you use feelings and not checks. A deadline takes away the time you need to ask a friend or look the offer up.
urgency.safe_response: Stop. A real job, bank or office will wait one day. Take your time, check by yourself and ask someone you trust.

sources.publisher: University of Cambridge Computer Laboratory (Stajano and Wilson, 2009)

authority.label: Authority
authority.definition: The scammer pretends to be someone you should obey, such as the police, a bank, an embassy, immigration or a licensed agency.
signs: Says they are from the police, a bank, an embassy, immigration or an agency
Official-looking logos, case numbers, badge numbers or certificates
Formal or legal words, and a tone that says you did something wrong
Passes you to a "senior officer" and does not let you hang up and check
authority.how_it_works: Most people are taught to follow officials and experts. A scammer borrows that trust, so you do what you are told and do not question it.
authority.safe_response: A title can be faked. Hang up and call the office yourself, using a number from its official website. Real officials never ask for OTPs, passwords or a money transfer.

sources.publisher: Montgomery County Police Department, Maryland, USA

scarcity.label: Scarcity
scarcity.definition: The scammer says there is very little left, such as a few jobs, visa slots or places, so you rush to take one.
signs: "Only 3 visa slots left" or "limited places"
A special offer for you only
"Others are waiting for your place"
The first person to pay gets the job
scarcity.how_it_works: People fear missing out on a rare chance. When a good job seems to be running out, you may pay before you check that it is real.
scarcity.safe_response: A good job or deal is still there tomorrow. If it only exists when you pay now, walk away.

sources.publisher: Montgomery County Police Department, Maryland, USA

fear.label: Fear
fear.definition: The scammer scares you with a threat, such as arrest, a fine, losing your job or visa, or a hacked account.
signs: Threats of arrest, a fine, or losing your job or visa
A claim that your bank account was hacked or will be closed
A threat to tell your employer or family
A threatening tone, or shouting in capital letters
fear.how_it_works: Fear makes it hard to think. A scared person wants the problem to go away fast, and the scammer offers a way out that costs money.
fear.safe_response: Fear is a push, not proof. Breathe, hang up and check with the real office. Authorities do not threaten arrest by chat or ask for payment by transfer.

reciprocity.label: Reciprocity
reciprocity.definition: The scammer does you a small favour or gives you a gift first, so you feel you owe them something back.
signs: Free help with forms, a visa or a job search
A small gift, or a small payment at the start of a task
"I helped you, now please help me"
Shares a "secret" tip to show that they trust you
reciprocity.how_it_works: People feel they should repay a kindness. The scammer gives a little first, then asks for much more, and it feels rude to say no.
reciprocity.safe_response: A favour does not mean you owe money. You can say no and stop. Be careful with anyone who helps you first and then asks for money.

sources.publisher: Montgomery County Police Department, Maryland, USA

social_proof.label: Social proof
social_proof.definition: The scammer shows that many other people joined, won or earned money, so the scam looks safe.
signs: Screenshots of people earning money or saying thank you
A group chat full of members who praise the offer
"Everyone from your town or community has joined"
Many reviews, likes or followers on a new account
A friend's hacked account that recommends the offer
social_proof.how_it_works: People copy what others do. Fake reviews and group chats make a scam look popular, so you trust it without checking.
social_proof.safe_response: Screenshots, likes and group chats can be faked. Check official lists, and ask people you know in person. Do not join only because others did.

sources.publisher: Montgomery County Police Department, Maryland, USA
University of Cambridge Computer Laboratory (Stajano and Wilson, 2009)
